newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ABN AMRO sees rand at 4.60 on dollar by year-end.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO sees rand at 4.60 on dollar by year-end.

text.p: The South African rand is likely to fall to 4.60 against the dollar by the end of 1996 but the currency should stabilise in 1997, according to Dutch bank ABN AMRO.

"Despite the sound economic fundamentals, there is little indication that the rand is about to rebound against the dollar, and we see a further slide of the currency to 4.60 at the year-end," economist Anastasia Gekis said in a report this week.

However, assuming that the government will succeed in implementing its macro-economic strategy, thus providing fundamental stability to the economy, the rand should not exhibit a strong downward trend next year.
The rand has shed around a quarter of its value against the dollar since mid-February. It was last trading at 4.5440/90 against the dollar.

Gekis said consumer price inflation would remain in single digits, peaking at a maximum nine percent early next year and decreasing again during the course of 1997 due to the continued tight monetary policy of the Reserve Bank.
The result should be an average inflation rate of 7.5 percent in both 1996 and 1997.
August consumer inflation stood at 7.5 percnet, up from 7.1 percent in July.
